title: Arque Systems launches €35m Q-STAR.NRW initiative to develop and integrate 200 qubit quantum computer
html:
Jülich-Aachen spin-off Arque Systems has launched Q-STAR.NRW, a €35 million ($38.4 million) initiative to develop and integrate a semiconductor-based quantum computer with up to 200 qubits.

The initiative will run until the end of 2029 and receive 90 percent of its funding from German federal funds under the Coal Regions Investment Act, with the final ten percent coming from the State of North Rhine-Westphalia via Forschungszentrum Jülich Supercomputing Center (FZJ).

Jülich-Aachen is itself a spin-off from Forschungszentrum Jülich and RWTH Aachen University.

The project builds on recent demonstrations from Arque Systems that saw the startup successfully integrate a five-qubit quantum computer into the Jülich UNified Infrastructure for Quantum Computing (JUNIQ). Under the Q-STAR.NRW initiative, FZJ and Arque will work to prove the technology can function on a larger scale by building a quantum computer with up to 200 qubits.

Once developed, the quantum computer will be integrated into JUNIQ, where it will be connected to classical high-performance systems. Alongside the hardware, the project partners are also developing the software, hybrid quantum algorithms, and services for user support and training.

JUNIQ provides quantum computing access to industry and academia.

“With Q-STAR.NRW, we are taking the next important step in integrating quantum computing into our European high-performance computing infrastructures,” said Prof. Dr. Kristel Michielsen, director, FZJ.

“It is crucial that we do not view quantum computers as isolated systems, but instead integrate them closely with classical supercomputers and enable their use in real-world scientific and industrial applications. Integrating the new semiconductor-based system into JUNIQ allows us to develop hybrid quantum-HPC workflows on a powerful and scalable platform and make them accessible to a broad user community.“
summary: Program run in partnership with Germany’s Forschungszentrum Jülich Supercomputing Center
